title: TenderNet v1.0.0: data and code for "Unconcentrated markets, captive buyers: incumbency in Türkiye's public IT procurement"
description:
Reproducibility package (code, derived data, data dictionary, paper sources) for Unconcentrated markets, captive buyers: incumbency in Türkiye's public IT procurement (F. Aksoy, A. Şimşek).

The data are 9,991 awarded IT contracts (main sample; 13,024 audited records in total) published on Türkiye's e-procurement platform EKAP between 2010 and 2026, linking 2,814 firms to 2,890 public buyers. Count-based supplier HHIs are below 1,000 in every product market, and value-based HHIs exceed 1,000 only in three small markets dominated by single contracts. Buyers nevertheless return to incumbents far more often than market structure implies: 45% of repeat-eligible contracts go to an incumbent, against 21% under a permutation null that fixes each buyer's demand and each firm's wins within product market, year and province (6% within market and year only). About a third of these contracts are annual re-tenders of the same service and carry most of the excess, but new needs still exceed their null (31% vs 16%). In a conditional-logit supplier-choice model with firm-activity and home-province controls, prior supply to the buyer multiplies a firm's odds of winning by about 24. Incumbency is highest in health information systems and under negotiated procedures without publication (Art. 21(b), Law 4734), where it jumped in 2017-18, and incumbent-won tenders attract single bids more often.

Code is released under the MIT License. The derived data (data/) are released under CC BY 4.0; the underlying records are public records published by the Public Procurement Authority (KİK) on EKAP under Law 4734. Names of natural persons are pseudonymized (KVKK, Law 6698).
notes: Derived data in data/ are licensed CC-BY-4.0 (see data/LICENSE); code is MIT. Underlying records: Kamu İhale Kurumu (KİK), EKAP, https://ekapv2.kik.gov.tr.
